core_step: List the papers directory to discover files to organize
why_essential: You must know which files exist (and count) before creating folders or classifying them

core_step: Create the five target subject folders
why_essential: Folders are required destinations for sorting files so each file can be moved into its correct subject

core_step: Prepare a brief on-disk plan and findings files for tracking the classification task
why_essential: A concise plan and findings file record the intended classification and serve as working memory for batch classification

core_step: Read/inspect each document (PDF/PPTX/DOCX) to determine its subject category
why_essential: Accurate classification requires reading document content (or extracting text) to assign each file to exactly one subject folder
evidence: Read/Extract operations for many files (e.g., "PDF file read: /root/papers/all/0704.0117v1.pdf", pptx slides extracted, docx document.xml extracted)

core_step: Run parallel classification agents to assign each file to one of the five categories
why_essential: Batch/agent classification produced the mapping of each of the 103 files to a specific subject folder, enabling bulk moves
evidence: Agent outputs showing JSON assignments for batches, e.g. [{"file": "0704.0117v1.pdf", "category": "trapped_ion_and_qc"}, ...]

core_step: Move each file from the source folder into its assigned subject folder
why_essential: Physically relocating files into the target folders completes the organization task; must preserve file names/content
evidence: mv commands moving lists of files into trapped_ion_and_qc, black_hole, DNA, music_history, LLM; shell reported e.g. 'trapped_ion_and_qc done'

core_step: Handle binary PPTX/DOCX by extracting text (or metadata) to classify them
why_essential: Non-PDF binary files must be inspected via appropriate extraction to determine their subject and ensure they are not left unclassified
evidence: python unzip/read of DAMOP.pptx and paper_file_1.docx/paper_file_2.docx to extract document.xml / slide XML content

core_step: Verify that the source directory is empty and count files in each subject folder
why_essential: A final verification ensures all files were moved and that every file belongs to exactly one subject folder (no leftovers)
evidence: Verification output: '=== Remaining in /all === 0' and folder counts: LLM 20, trapped_ion_and_qc 23, black_hole 20, DNA 20, music_history 20

core_step: Report completion and summary of file distribution
why_essential: A final status message confirms successful task completion and provides a concise summary for the user
evidence: All 103 files have been successfully organized... 'All 103 files have been successfully organized. The `/all` folder is now empty and files are distributed as...'
